clips.send: Cell: heart muscle cell. Basic unit of structure and function. The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all the activities of life. This heart muscle cell is long and striped. The stripes are protein fibers that shorten to make the cell contract. Like all animal cells it has a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus, but no cell wall.

clips.send: Stage. Holds the slide. The flat platform where you put the slide. The hole in the middle lets light pass up through the specimen. The specimen must be thin so light can shine through it.
clips.text: Stage. Holds the slide. The flat platform where you put the slide.. The hole in the middle lets light pass up through the specimen.. The specimen must be thin so light can shine through it.

clips.send: Tissue: heart muscle. Similar cells with one job. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to do the same job. Animals have 4 main tissue types: muscle, nervous, epithelial and connective tissue. Heart muscle cells are branched and linked end to end, so they contract together as one team.

Animals have 4 main tissue types: muscle, nervous, epithelial and connective tissue.. Heart muscle cells are branched and linked end to end, so they contract together as one team.

clips.send: Organ: the heart. Several tissues working together. An organ is a structure made of two or more kinds of tissue that work together for a specific job. The heart contains muscle tissue (to pump), nervous tissue (to control the beat), connective tissue and epithelial tissue (lining). Your heart beats about 100,000 times every day.

clips.send: Coarse adjustment knob. Big focus moves. The large knob moves the stage up or down a lot. Use it only with the LOW-power objective to find the image. On high power it could crash the long objective into the slide.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A tissue has one main kind of cell. An organ has several kinds of tissue.
clips.text: Common mix-up: A tissue has one main kind of cell. An organ has several kinds of tissue.

clips.send: Organ system. Organs working together. An organ system is a group of organs that work together to do one big job. The circulatory system equals heart + blood vessels + blood. It carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell. Systems also team up: the respiratory system brings in oxygen, and the circulatory system delivers it.

clips.send: Diaphragm. Controls how much light. Opening the diaphragm lets in more light; closing it makes the view dimmer but often clearer for see-through cells. At high power the view gets darker, so you may need to open the diaphragm.

clips.send: Theodor Schwann. A zoologist who showed that ALL animals are made of cells too. With Schleiden he proposed that cells are the basic unit of all living things.
clips.text: Theodor Schwann. A zoologist who showed that ALL animals are made of cells too. With Schleiden he proposed that cells are the basic unit of all living things.

clips.send: Rudolf Virchow. A doctor who stated “Omnis cellula e cellula”: every cell comes from another cell. (He built on observations of cell division by Robert Remak.)
clips.text: Rudolf Virchow. A doctor who stated “Omnis cellula e cellula”: every cell comes from another cell. (He built on observations of cell division by Robert Remak.)

clips.send: Arm. Holds the top and is used to carry it. Carry a microscope with two hands: one hand on the arm, the other under the base. The arm connects the body tube to the base.
clips.text: Arm. Holds the top and is used to carry it. Carry a microscope with two hands: one hand on the arm, the other under the base.. The arm connects the body tube to the base.

clips.send: Eyepiece (ocular lens). The lens you look through. The eyepiece usually magnifies 10 times . Total magnification equals eyepiece power times objective power. 10 times times 40 times equals 400 times .
clips.text: Eyepiece (ocular lens). The lens you look through. The eyepiece usually magnifies 10×.. Total magnification = eyepiece power × objective power. 10× × 40× = 400×.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Bigger organisms do not have bigger cells. They have MORE cells.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Bigger organisms do not have bigger cells. They have MORE cells.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Plants have organs too (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit, seed), but plants are usually NOT described as having “organ systems” like animals do.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Plants have organs too (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit, seed), but plants are usually NOT described as having “organ systems” like animals do.

clips.send: Organelle: mitochondrion. Releases energy for the cell. Organelles are tiny structures inside a cell, each with its own job, like the nucleus, mitochondria and ribosomes. Mitochondria release energy from food by cellular respiration. The folded inner membrane gives more space for this work. Heart muscle cells are packed with mitochondria because the heart never stops working.

clips.send: Fine adjustment knob. Small focus moves. The small knob moves the stage just a tiny bit to make the image sharp. At high power (40 times ), use ONLY the fine knob.

clips.send: Base. Supports the microscope. The heavy bottom keeps the microscope steady. Support the base with one hand whenever you carry the microscope.

clips.send: Common mix-up: An elephant is bigger than a mouse NOT because its cells are bigger, but because it has far MORE cells! Most animal cells are about the same size.
clips.text: Common mix-up: An elephant is bigger than a mouse NOT because its cells are bigger, but because it has far MORE cells! Most animal cells are about the same size.

clips.send: Stage clips. Hold the slide still. Two metal clips press the slide flat so it does not slide around.

clips.send: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek. Ground amazing single lenses (up to about 270 times ) and became the first person to see LIVING cells: tiny swimming “animalcules” in pond water, and later bacteria and blood cells.
clips.text: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek. Ground amazing single lenses (up to about 270×) and became the first person to see LIVING cells: tiny swimming “animalcules” in pond water, and later bacteria and blood cells.

clips.send: Common mix-up: “Cell” is the smallest LIVING level. Organelles are parts of a cell; they cannot live on their own.
clips.text: Common mix-up: “Cell” is the smallest LIVING level. Organelles are parts of a cell; they cannot live on their own.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Higher magnification does not show MORE of the slide. It shows a smaller area, but bigger.

clips.send: Revolving nosepiece. Switches objective lenses. Turn it to click a different objective lens into place. Always turn the nosepiece itself, not the objective lenses.
clips.text: Revolving nosepiece. Switches objective lenses. Turn it to click a different objective lens into place.. Always turn the nosepiece itself, not the objective lenses.

clips.send: Body tube. Connects eyepiece and objectives. Light travels up through the body tube to your eye. It holds the lenses at the right distance apart.
clips.text: Body tube. Connects eyepiece and objectives. Light travels up through the body tube to your eye.. It holds the lenses at the right distance apart.

clips.send: Organism. A whole living thing. An organism is a complete living thing that can carry out all life processes on its own. A human body is made of about 37 trillion cells, more than 200 kinds of them. A unicellular organism (like a bacterium or paramecium) is just ONE cell, so for it the cell level and the organism level are the same.

clips.send: Robert Hooke. Looked at a thin slice of cork with his microscope and saw rows of tiny empty boxes. They reminded him of small rooms, so he named them “cells”.
clips.text: Robert Hooke. Looked at a thin slice of cork with his microscope and saw rows of tiny empty boxes. They reminded him of small rooms, so he named them “cells”.

clips.send: Light source. Shines light up through the slide. A compound microscope needs light to pass THROUGH the specimen. Older microscopes use a mirror (反光镜) to reflect light instead of a lamp.

clips.send: Common mix-up: The “cells” Hooke saw were only the empty walls of dead cork cells. The first person to see LIVING cells was Leeuwenhoek.
clips.text: Common mix-up: The “cells” Hooke saw were only the empty walls of dead cork cells. The first person to see LIVING cells was Leeuwenhoek.

clips.send: Matthias Schleiden. A botanist who studied many plant parts and concluded that ALL plants are made of cells.
clips.text: Matthias Schleiden. A botanist who studied many plant parts and concluded that ALL plants are made of cells.

clips.send: Objective lenses. Main magnifying lenses. Most school microscopes have 4 times (low), 10 times (medium) and 40 times (high) objectives. Higher-power objectives are LONGER, so they come very close to the slide. Always start with the lowest-power objective: it shows the largest area and is easiest to focus.

clips.send: 施旺。动物学家，证明所有动物也都是由细胞构成的。他和施莱登一起提出：细胞是一切生物的基本单位。

clips.send: 器官系统。多个器官协同工作。器官系统（简称系统）是由几个器官共同完成一项重要生理功能而组成的。循环系统 等于 心脏 + 血管 + 血液，负责把氧气和营养物质运送到每一个细胞。系统之间也会合作：呼吸系统吸入氧气，循环系统再把氧气送到全身。

clips.send: 列文虎克。磨制出非常好的单片透镜（可放大约 270 倍），成为第一个看到“活细胞”的人：他在池塘水中看到游动的“小动物”，后来还看到了细菌和血细胞。

clips.send: 罗伯特·胡克。用自制的显微镜观察一片很薄的软木，看到许多排列整齐的小空格。它们让他想起小房间，于是他把它们命名为“细胞”。

clips.send: 细准焦螺旋。小幅度升降，使物像更清晰。小螺旋只让载物台（或镜筒）微微升降，让物像更清晰。在高倍（40 乘 ）下，只能用细准焦螺旋。

clips.send: 细胞器：线粒体。为细胞释放能量。细胞器是细胞内的微小结构，各有分工，例如细胞核、线粒体和核糖体。线粒体通过呼吸作用把食物中的能量释放出来。它的内膜向内折叠，增大了工作面积。心肌细胞里线粒体特别多，因为心脏一刻不停地工作。

clips.send: 目镜。你用眼睛看的镜头。目镜通常放大 10 倍。放大倍数 等于 目镜倍数 乘 物镜倍数，例如 10 乘 乘 40 乘 等于 400 乘 。

clips.send: 光源。从下往上照亮玻片。复式显微镜需要光线“穿过”标本。老式显微镜没有灯，而是用反光镜把光反射上来。

clips.send: 细胞：心肌细胞。结构和功能的基本单位。细胞是能独立完成生命活动的最小单位。心肌细胞细长，上面有横纹。这些横纹是能缩短的蛋白质纤维，让细胞收缩。和所有动物细胞一样，它有细胞膜、细胞质和细胞核，但没有细胞壁。
clips.text: 细胞：心肌细胞. 结构和功能的基本单位. 细胞是能独立完成生命活动的最小单位。. 心肌细胞细长，上面有横纹。这些横纹是能缩短的蛋白质纤维，让细胞收缩。. 和所有动物细胞一样，它有细胞膜、细胞质和细胞核，但没有细胞壁。

clips.send: 生物体。一个完整的生物。生物体是能够独立完成各项生命活动的完整生命。人体大约由 37 万亿个细胞组成，细胞种类超过 200 种。单细胞生物（如细菌、草履虫）只有一个细胞，所以对它来说，细胞就是整个生物体。
clips.text: 生物体. 一个完整的生物. 生物体是能够独立完成各项生命活动的完整生命。. 人体大约由 37 万亿个细胞组成，细胞种类超过 200 种。. 单细胞生物（如细菌、草履虫）只有一个细胞，所以对它来说，细胞就是整个生物体。

clips.send: 组织：心肌组织。形态相似、功能相同的细胞群。组织是由形态相似、结构和功能相同的细胞联合在一起形成的细胞群。动物有四种基本组织：肌肉组织、神经组织、上皮组织和结缔组织。心肌细胞有分支，首尾相连，所以它们能一起收缩、协调跳动。
clips.text: 组织：心肌组织. 形态相似、功能相同的细胞群. 组织是由形态相似、结构和功能相同的细胞联合在一起形成的细胞群。. 动物有四种基本组织：肌肉组织、神经组织、上皮组织和结缔组织。. 心肌细胞有分支，首尾相连，所以它们能一起收缩、协调跳动。

clips.send: 器官：心脏。由几种组织构成。器官是由不同的组织按照一定的次序结合在一起，能完成一定功能的结构。心脏含有肌肉组织（收缩泵血）、神经组织（控制心跳）、结缔组织和上皮组织（内表面）。你的心脏每天跳动大约 10 万次。

clips.send: 容易混淆：大象比老鼠大，并不是因为大象的细胞更大，而是因为它的细胞多得多！大多数动物细胞的大小都差不多。

clips.send: 物镜。主要的放大镜头。大多数学校显微镜有 4 乘 （低倍）、10 乘 （中倍）、40 乘 （高倍）物镜。物镜倍数越高，镜头越长，离玻片越近。总是先用低倍物镜：它看到的范围最大，也最容易对焦。

clips.send: 镜座。稳稳地支撑显微镜。沉重的底座让显微镜放得稳。搬运时一只手要托住镜座。

clips.send: 魏尔肖。一位医生，提出“细胞来自细胞”（Omnis cellula e cellula）：所有细胞都来自已有的细胞。（他借鉴了雷马克对细胞分裂的观察。）

clips.send: 压片夹。把玻片固定住。两个金属夹把玻片压住，防止它滑动。
clips.text: 压片夹. 把玻片固定住. 两个金属夹把玻片压住，防止它滑动。

clips.send: 光圈（遮光器）。调节光线强弱。光圈开大，光线变强；光圈调小，视野变暗，但透明的细胞往往看得更清楚。换高倍物镜后视野变暗，可以把光圈开大一些。

clips.send: 容易混淆：植物也有器官（根、茎、叶、花、果实、种子），但植物通常没有像动物那样的“系统”这一层次。
clips.text: 容易混淆：植物也有器官（根、茎、叶、花、果实、种子），但植物通常没有像动物那样的“系统”这一层次。

clips.send: 施莱登。植物学家，研究了大量植物结构后得出结论：所有植物都是由细胞构成的。

clips.send: 转换器。用来更换物镜。转动它，让另一个物镜“咔”一声对准通光孔。要转动转换器本身，不要直接扳物镜。

clips.send: 容易混淆：个体大的生物，细胞并不更大，而是细胞数量更多。

clips.send: 镜筒。连接目镜和物镜。光线沿着镜筒向上传到你的眼睛。它让目镜和物镜保持合适的距离。

clips.send: 容易混淆：放大倍数越高，看到的并不是更多，而是更小的范围被放得更大。

clips.send: 容易混淆：细胞是最小的“活”的层次。细胞器只是细胞的组成部分，不能单独存活。
